:::{#thm-mutual-information-kl}
#### Mutual information as a divergence

Let $X$ and $Y$ be [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
with [joint probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf) $p(x, y)$
and [marginal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-marginal) [probability mass functions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $p(x)$ and $p(y)$.
If their entropies are finite, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
then their [mutual information](#def-mutual-information) is the
[Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence)
of the product of the marginals from the joint distribution: <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

$$I(X; Y) = \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log \frac{p(x, y)}{p(x) \, p(y)},$$

where the sum runs over the pairs with $p(x, y) > 0$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::

::: {.proof}

The entropies are finite, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
so the expectations below are finite and can be split and regrouped.
With probability $1$, $p(X, Y) > 0$, $p(X) > 0$ and $p(Y) > 0$.
By @def-mutual-information and the definitions of
[entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy)
and [joint entropy](#def-joint-entropy),

$$
\begin{aligned}
I(X; Y)
&= \entropyf{X} + \entropyf{Y} - \entropyf{X, Y} \\
&= \E{-\log p(X)} + \E{-\log p(Y)} - \E{-\log p(X, Y)} \\
&= \E{\log p(X, Y) - \log p(X) - \log p(Y)} \\
&= \E{\log \frac{p(X, Y)}{p(X) \, p(Y)}} \\
&= \sum_{x, y} p(x, y) \log \frac{p(x, y)}{p(x) \, p(y)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The last line is the definition of expectation over the pairs with $p(x, y) > 0$. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
It is the divergence of $p(x) \, p(y)$ from $p(x, y)$ <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
by the [discrete formula](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-kl-divergence-discrete).

:::
